transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Supreme Court has blocked the use of a Missouri congressional map backed by President
Trump.
St. Louis Public Radio's Jason Rosenbaum reports it's a setback to Republican efforts to keep
control of the House.
The high court stayed an appeals court decision that required Missouri to use a map aimed
at ousting Democratic Congressman Emanuel Cleaver.
Instead, Missouri voters will use congressional lines passed four years ago that include a
safe seat for Cleaver.
Missouri Republicans targeted Cleaver at the behest of Trump to prevent the GOP from losing
control of the House, but redistricting opponents gathered enough signatures to prevent the
Trump-backed map from going into effect.
Republicans hold a slim majority in the U.S. House, so barring any more rulings in what
has been a process with many turns, the ruling could help Democrats win control of the chamber.
For NPR News, I'm Jason Rosenbaum in St. Louis.
Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped up his state visit to the U.S. today.
Little was announced outside the promise of more meetings, and China agreeing to extend
their trade war truce until January.
And Piers, Rob Schmitz has more on what's happened since the truce began.
In that time, the Trump administration largely shifted its focus away from China.
It started a war of choice with Iran.
That's led to higher oil and gas prices worldwide.
Now, the Trump administration says it's making the world a safer place from a potentially
nuclear-armed Iran.
But in this time since the truce with Beijing was made, the U.S. and China have not made
much progress on key issues like rare-earth materials, managing A.I., regional issues
like the South China Sea, Taiwan.
NPR's Rob Schmitz reporting Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume
talks on its nuclear program in seven days.
That's if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade, waves sanctions on Iranian oil sales, and
observes a ceasefire that would include Lebanon.
The deal strongly resembles the so-called memorandum of understanding reached in June
that collapsed as Iran resumed attacks on shipping in the strait.
A powerful nor'easter is expected to wallop parts of the East Coast this weekend with
heavy rain and high winds.
Ocean state media's David Wright reports from Rhode Island.
Nor'easters tend to be winter events here in New England.
It's a storm much like a hurricane, except that it doesn't come up from the tropics.
This one is forecast to linger for days.
Sean Lacy, town manager in Westerly, Rhode Island, is urging residents to batten down
the hatches.
You're going to get a lot of rain.
You're going to get wind.
If you have outside patio furniture, try and secure it or bring it inside.
Do everything you can to secure the items in your yard, as you would any other type
of wind event storm.
Power outages are expected, too, as gale force winds topple trees.
Fall foliage hasn't really begun yet, so those trees full of leaves are even more vulnerable
to the storm.
For NPR News, I'm David Wright in Westerly, Rhode Island.
Major U.S. stock indexes rose today.
This is NPR.
A New Mexico jury has found Facebook liable of deceiving users about privacy protections
on the social media platform.
It's now up to the judge to determine how much the company would pay.
The trial centered on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming
from a third-party personality quiz.
Pope Leo is in the midst of a series of speeches across France, and PR's Eleanor Beardsley
reports it's the first papal visit to France since 2008.
French television is covering the Pope's visit live, showing him being greeted by President
Macron, officers of the French military, and dozens of school children on a red carpet on
the airport tarmac as he stepped off his plane.
In an opening speech to Macron, diplomats at the Elise Palace, Leo raised existential
questions about scientific progress, life, and human rights.
He warned that a, quote, "paradise of machines" risks undermining humanity.
The Pope will greet the faithful in the streets of Paris before heading to Notre Dame Cathedral.
This evening, he is holding a sold-out mass at the Stade de France, Paris' major sports
stadium.
There is huge fervor for his visit in a country that's both traditionally Catholic and staunchly
secular.
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Paris.
It's Dolly Parton Day, that's right, September 25th, or 9 to 5.
Parton left a legacy as a singer, songwriter, actor, philanthropist, and entrepreneur.
And after her death last month at age 80, several cities and states are establishing
today as their Dolly Parton Day.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Supreme Court blocks Missouri congressional map backed by Trump, preserving Democratic seat
Chinese President Xi Jinping concludes U.S. state visit with trade war truce extension
Trump administration shifts focus from China to Iran conflict since trade truce began
Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within seven days
Powerful nor'easter expected to hit East Coast this weekend with rain and high winds
New Mexico jury finds Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections
Pope Francis begins multi-day visit to France, first papal visit since 2008
Dolly Parton commemorated with official day in multiple cities and states after death
